s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive back pain and lower limb weakness with evidence of spinal injury
salient_findings: L5 burst fracture with canal compromise
key_facts: 28-year-old man
Uses a wheelchair
Severe back pain for two weeks
Inability to walk for two weeks
Mild back pain after pulling a rug one month earlier
Progressive intensification of back pain
Bodybuilding with use of licensed and unlicensed substances
No significant trauma
Severe left and moderate right weakness of the extensor hallucis longus muscles
Moderate weakness of ankle dorsiflexors bilaterally
Normal quadriceps and ankle plantarflexion strength
Intact sphincter function
Elevated C-reactive protein level
L2 compression fracture on plain radiographs
L5 burst fracture with canal compromise on plain radiographs
Intravertebral vacuum cleft at L5 on plain radiographs
T2-weighted “double line sign” at L5 on MRI

shortlist.label: Kummell disease
shortlist.why_kept: Intravertebral vacuum cleft and vertebral compression fractures are characteristic of Kummell disease

shortlist.label: Osteoporosis
shortlist.why_kept: Compression fractures and elevated C-reactive protein level are consistent with osteoporosis

shortlist.label: Vertebral osteonecrosis
shortlist.why_kept: T2-weighted "double line sign" on MRI is a specific finding for vertebral osteonecrosis

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated C-reactive protein level and compression fractures could be indicative of multiple myeloma

shortlist.label: Bone metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Compression fractures and elevated C-reactive protein level could be consistent with bone metastasis

raw.rationale: The presence of an intravertebral vacuum cleft and a 'double line sign' on MRI, along with a compression fracture and elevated C-reactive protein, are characteristic of Kummell disease, which is a type of vertebral osteonecrosis often associated with vertebral compression fractures.

rejected.label: Osteoporosis
rejected.why: While osteoporosis could contribute to the compression fractures, it does not fully explain the acute progression of symptoms or the specific imaging findings like the intravertebral vacuum cleft.

rejected.label: Vertebral osteonecrosis
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes Kummell disease, but Kummell disease is more specific and better explains the combination of clinical and imaging findings in this case.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: There is no mention of systemic symptoms, significant anemia, hypercalcemia, or other specific findings typical of multiple myeloma, and the bone scan did not show widespread disease.

rejected.label: Bone metastasis
rejected.why: The absence of a known primary malignancy and the localized nature of the findings on the bone scan make this diagnosis less likely.
